description: Seed cases for manual model-review evaluation. Findings require human adjudication before scoring.

cases.title: Refund handling change
cases.context: Existing order.balance is an integer remaining balance. Successful refund decrements it and pays amount.
cases.diff:
def refund(order, amount):
+    if amount <= 0: raise ValueError()
+    order.balance -= amount
+    pay_customer(amount)

cases.context: The user may explicitly configure a timeout of 0 to disable the wait. Previous code returned the configured value directly.

+ const timeout = settings.timeout || 30;

cases.context: Previously: message Event { string user_id = 1; string reason = 2; }. Historical events are still stored.

cases.context: The database driver supports placeholders, and parameterized requests are the project convention.

+ cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = %s', (user_id,))

cases.context: The code is called with integer inputs only. Previous implementation: return x * 2.
cases.diff:
- return x * 2
+ return x + x

cases.title: Python utility module update
cases.context: A Python utility module receives a new comment and a small helper function.
cases.diff:

+ def total(items): return sum(items)

cases.title: Turn error code rename
cases.context: Operators find failed turns by searching the session journal for the code that journal_code returns. A duplicate call identifier is reported as TurnError::InvalidCall, and a call denied by a preference as TurnError::Denied. The docs page lists those codes.

cases.title: New refusal record and downgrade note
cases.context: Older builds treat a journal holding a record type they don't know as corrupt and then fail every tool call. The writer rotates the active file into numbered archives and keeps the newest four.

cases.title: Recoverable rejection of invalid tool arguments
cases.context: Model output reaches parse_call through two provider adapters. The chat-completions adapter copies function.arguments into RawCall.arguments as received, whatever its JSON type. The responses adapter builds RawCall with `let arguments = item["arguments"].as_str().ok_or(ProviderError::MalformedResponse)?;` and any ProviderError ends the turn. The change is meant to let the model retry after any call whose arguments are invalid.

cases.title: Test for replaying a rejected tool call
cases.context: SessionJournal::open(path) loads a session from disk. fixture.run(&journal, model) runs one turn against an already open journal and appends its events. The test is meant to prove that a rejected call and its result are restored into history when a session is loaded again.

cases.title: Tool argument limit documentation
cases.context: argument_limit is the only place the argument size limit is chosen; the docs page describes the limits to users.

cases.title: Recoverable result for rejected tool calls
cases.context: Operators may set result_limit, the largest tool result sent back to the model, as low as 200 bytes; a result over the limit ends the turn. Call IDs may be up to 128 bytes and tool names up to 32. workspace_run_command and the other non-text tools take a 4 KiB argument limit; only create, edit and multi-edit take 32 KiB. rejection_result builds the result for every rejected call.

cases.title: Larger session event limit
cases.context: Builds before 0.63.0 refuse to open a session journal that holds any line over 64 KiB. Each journal line is one serialized event; serde_json writes every control character inside a string as a six-byte \u00XX escape. Message text is capped before encoding.

cases.title: Duplicate call error code
cases.context: The CLI prints ErrorKind::code() as error.code in its JSON output. The session journal separately records TurnError::journal_code(). A duplicate call identifier is reported as TurnError::InvalidCall, and a call denied by a preference as TurnError::Denied. docs/cli.md describes the CLI's JSON output.

cases.title: Arch Linux PKGBUILD subcommand for the release tool
cases.context: tools/release.py is a release helper that only the release workflow runs; that job holds no secrets. .github/workflows/sonar.yml runs SonarQube Cloud on every pull request, and the project fixes every new alert before merging. `git log -- tools/release.py` shows commit db7f3d7, whose message reads: "append-notice (Sonar S8707): It takes no file arguments. It reads the shared notices from .local/release/notices and writes the Windows-only notices file." tools/matrix_restart.py has `_inside_local(path)`, which resolves a path and raises unless it is under ROOT/.local.
cases.diff:
--- a/tools/release.py
+++ b/tools/release.py
@@
+def arch_pkgbuild(root, deb, output):
+    """Write output/PKGBUILD from tools/arch/PKGBUILD.in and copy the .deb beside it."""
+    deb, output = Path(deb), Path(output)
+    if not DEB_NAME.fullmatch(deb.name):
+        raise ReleaseError(f"not a release .deb: {deb.name}")
+    output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    template = (root / "tools" / "arch" / "PKGBUILD.in").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    (output / "PKGBUILD").write_text(render(template, deb), encoding="utf-8")
+    shutil.copyfile(deb, output / deb.name)
@@ def main(argv=None):
     append = commands.add_parser("append-notice", help="write the notices plus the libwebrtc licence texts")
     append.add_argument("--platform", required=True, choices=sorted(NOTICE_PLATFORMS))
+    arch = commands.add_parser("arch-pkgbuild", help="write a PKGBUILD that repackages the x86_64 .deb")
+    arch.add_argument("--deb", required=True, help="the x86_64 .deb from the Linux release job")
+    arch.add_argument("--output", required=True, help="directory for PKGBUILD and the copy of the .deb")
@@
+        if args.command == "arch-pkgbuild":
+            arch_pkgbuild(root, args.deb, args.output)
--- a/.github/workflows/release.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/release.yml
+      - run: python tools/release.py arch-pkgbuild --deb .local/release/arch/in/persephone.deb --output .local/release/arch/build

cases.title: Process billing queue messages
cases.context: worker.py consumes the billing queue. A message that is not deleted within the queue's 30-second visibility timeout becomes visible again and is delivered to another worker. payments.charge() calls the card provider, can take up to 90 seconds when the provider is slow, and sends no idempotency key. orders.mark_paid() sets status to 'paid'.
cases.diff:
--- a/billing/worker.py
+++ b/billing/worker.py
@@ def run(queue):
     for msg in queue.receive(wait_seconds=20):
-        log.info("skipping billing message %s", msg.id)
+        body = json.loads(msg.body)
+        order = orders.get(body["order_id"])
+        if order.status == "paid":
+            msg.delete()
+            continue
+        payments.charge(order.customer_id, order.total_cents)
+        orders.mark_paid(order.id)
+        msg.delete()

cases.title: Keep the product view up to date
cases.context: The product-updated topic delivers at least once and may deliver messages for the same product out of order. Every message carries the product's version, which the catalogue service increments on each change. A handler that returns an error has its message redelivered.
cases.diff:
--- a/catalog/projection.go
+++ b/catalog/projection.go
@@
+func (h *Handler) OnProductUpdated(ctx context.Context, m ProductUpdated) error {
+	_, err := h.db.ExecContext(ctx, `
+		INSERT INTO product_view (id, name, price_cents, version)
+		VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4)
+		ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE
+		SET name = EXCLUDED.name, price_cents = EXCLUDED.price_cents, version = EXCLUDED.version
+		WHERE product_view.version < EXCLUDED.version`,
+		m.ID, m.Name, m.PriceCents, m.Version)
+	return err
+}

cases.title: Price the cart on the server
cases.context: payments.createCharge({ amount, currency, customer }) takes amount as an integer in the currency's smallest unit (cents for USD) and rejects non-integers. products.price is a NUMERIC(10,2) column holding US dollars; the pg driver returns NUMERIC values as strings such as "19.99". The shop sells only in USD. validateCart(), called before checkout, rejects carts that name a product not in the products table.

cases.title: Show the signup conversion rate
cases.context: The internal admin dashboard shows the week's signup conversion rate. visits and signups are integer counts; the value is only displayed, never stored or used in a calculation.
cases.diff:
--- a/admin/metrics.py
+++ b/admin/metrics.py
@@
+def conversion_rate(signups: int, visits: int) -> float:
+    """Percentage of visits that ended in a signup, to one decimal place."""
+    if visits == 0:
+        return 0.0
+    return round(100 * signups / visits, 1)

cases.title: Let idle workers pick up abandoned jobs
cases.context: Workers on different hosts share a jobs table. A worker that claims a job sets lease_expires_at to its own clock plus 10 seconds and renews it every 8 seconds while it works. Hosts sync time with NTP; the infrastructure runbook records skews of several seconds after VM migrations. Two workers running the same job send its notifications twice.
cases.diff:
--- a/jobs/lease.py
+++ b/jobs/lease.py
@@
+def try_take_over(job_id: int) -> bool:
+    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
+    taken = db.session.execute(
+        update(Job)
+        .where(Job.id == job_id, Job.lease_expires_at < now)
+        .values(worker_id=WORKER_ID, lease_expires_at=now + timedelta(seconds=10))
+    ).rowcount
+    db.session.commit()
+    return taken == 1

cases.title: Let browsers cache exchange rates
cases.context: GET /api/rates returns the day's currency exchange rates from a public feed. The endpoint requires no authentication, reads no cookies and returns the same body to every caller; the rates change once a day.

cases.title: Let users change their email address
cases.context: Users stay signed in with a session cookie set with HttpOnly and Secure and no SameSite attribute. requireSession loads the session from that cookie. StartEmailChange emails a confirmation link to the new address; once the link is opened, that address becomes the account's email and receives its password-reset links.

cases.title: Export profiles for a list of users
cases.context: POST /exports accepts up to 10,000 user IDs. profileClient.get() calls the profile service, which allows 50 concurrent requests per client and answers 429 Too Many Requests beyond that; profileClient does not retry, and a 429 makes get() reject.

cases.title: Run the job worker inside the API process
cases.context: The service runs on Kubernetes; each deploy sends SIGTERM and kills the pod 30 seconds later. queue.Pop removes a job from a Redis list and returns it; nothing puts a job back. Processing a job takes up to 2 minutes.

cases.title: Deep-merge user options
cases.context: package.json declares "license": "MIT". The package is published to npm, and its README invites use in closed-source commercial applications. DEFAULTS and the options callers pass hold only JSON values: strings, numbers, booleans, null, arrays and plain objects.

cases.title: Stop returning email addresses from /users
cases.context: The PR description says: 'Stop returning email addresses in the public /users JSON response.' The handler encodes userpb.User values with encoding/json. +def export_report(report, path, compress=False, overwrite=False, include_hidden=False):

cases.title: Extract uploaded archives automatically
cases.context: handle_upload calls suggest_and_extract for any signed-in user's uploaded file, in the web worker. The worker's environment holds the database URL and the cloud storage credentials. client is an Anthropic API client.
cases.diff:
--- a/uploads/extract.py
+++ b/uploads/extract.py
@@
+def suggest_and_extract(upload_path: str) -> None:
+    kind = subprocess.run(["file", "-b", upload_path], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
+    head = Path(upload_path).read_bytes()[:2000].decode("utf-8", "replace")
+    prompt = (
+        f"File type: {kind} First bytes: {head} "
+        "Reply with only a shell command that extracts this archive into ./out."
+    )
+    reply = client.messages.create(
+        model="claude-sonnet-5-5",
+        max_tokens=200,
+        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
+    )
+    subprocess.run(reply.content[0].text, shell=True, cwd=WORK_DIR, check=True)

cases.title: Serve churn scores over HTTP
cases.context: train.py builds the model's features with features.build(df), which fills a missing income with the training-set median saved in artifacts/stats.json and then applies the scaler saved in artifacts/scaler.pkl, in the column order age, income, tenure_months. MODEL is loaded once at startup. About 30% of requests omit income.
cases.diff:
--- a/serve.py
+++ b/serve.py
@@
+class ScoreRequest(BaseModel):
+    age: int
+    income: float | None = None
+    tenure_months: int
+
+
+@app.post("/score")
+def score():
+    try:
+        req = ScoreRequest.model_validate(request.get_json())
+    except ValidationError as e:
+        return {"error": e.errors()}, 400
+    x = np.array([[req.age, req.income or 0, req.tenure_months]])
+    return {"score": float(MODEL.predict_proba(x)[0, 1])}
